title_plain: Navigating ASON Texts -- Cleft Sentences and Relative Clauses in Regulation Language
menu_desc: Compliance, jurisdiction and enforcement, and the two structures that decide which noun a clause is talking about -- 35 slides
hero_line: In a regulation, the hardest question is never what. It is which one.
grammar_point: cleft sentences and relative clauses with prepositions

provoke.h: Which One Does the Clause Belong To?
provoke.quote: The port authority to which the vessel was registered issued a warning.
provoke.src: Written for this lesson -- one sentence with a deliberate error of reference
provoke.task: The sentence is grammatically well formed and factually impossible: a vessel is not registered to a port authority. Say which noun the clause should be attached to. The paper builds whole questions on exactly this.

goals: what the writer chose to put first
which noun the relative clause is about

vocab.def: the state of doing what a rule or a convention requires
vocab.ex: The vessel was found to be in compliance with the provision.

vocab.def: legal responsibility for damage, loss or injury
vocab.ex: It is the flag state that bears liability for the certificate it issued.

vocab.def: the legal authority a state has over a place, a ship or a person
vocab.ex: The vessel comes under the jurisdiction of the state whose flag she flies.

vocab.def: an official change made to a text that is already in force
vocab.ex: The amendment entered into force eighteen months after adoption.

vocab.def: the formal act by which a state accepts to be bound by a treaty
vocab.ex: Ratification by thirty states was required before the annex applied.

vocab.def: a section added to a convention, carrying its detailed technical rules
vocab.ex: The technical requirements are set out in the annex, not in the articles.

vocab.def: a binding international agreement between states, such as SOLAS
vocab.ex: The convention sets out the responsibilities of flag states.

vocab.def: a later instrument that adds to or modifies an existing convention
vocab.ex: The protocol of 1988 replaced the survey regime of the original text.

vocab.def: one specific clause or requirement inside a legal text
vocab.ex: Enforcement of the provision falls to the port state.

vocab.def: the act of making sure a rule is actually obeyed, with consequences if not
vocab.ex: Enforcement is what separates a ratified convention from a real one.

reading_sub: Where the duty sits when three legal systems all touch the same hull

paras: A convention does not become law because it is adopted. What makes it law in any particular ship is ratification by the state whose flag she flies, followed by transposition into that state's own legislation. It is for that reason that two identical vessels, side by side at the same berth, may be subject to different provisions of the same instrument.

The vessel in this case was registered in a state which had ratified the convention but not the protocol that replaced its survey regime. The classification society to which the owner had contracted the surveys held an authorisation from that flag state and from no other. The port authority in whose waters she lay was acting for a state which had ratified both instruments, and whose inspectors were therefore applying a standard the ship had never been built to meet.

It was not the surveyor who was at fault, and it was not the master. What produced the detention was an amendment that one registry had accepted and the other had not, and a certificate that was valid under the law of the flag and insufficient under the law of the port. Both readings were correct. Only one of them was enforceable in that harbour.

The case is cited whenever the industry discusses jurisdiction, because it shows what compliance actually costs. Liability did not follow the fault; it followed the flag. And enforcement, which is the only part of the system the master can see from the bridge, belonged to the state that had done nothing at all except open its port.

grammar_question: The first two point at ONE thing and push everything else out of the frame. The last two attach a clause to a noun that is not the nearest one. For each of the four, say what would be lost if you wrote it in ordinary order.
grammar_rows: the it-cleft: it names X and excludes everything else
It was not the surveyor who was at fault.
the wh-cleft: it delays X to the end, where the emphasis falls
What produced the detention was an amendment.
formal relative clause: the preposition moves to the front with the pronoun
the society to which the owner had contracted the surveys
possession inside the clause; it can belong to a thing, not only to a person

the relative clause does NOT always attach to the nearest noun. The port authority in whose waters she lay was acting for a state which had ratified both -- which points at the state, not at the waters and not at the authority. Every wrong option re-attaches the clause to the wrong noun.
grammar_insight: Both structures exist to control where the reader looks. The cleft says look here and nowhere else; the relative clause says this one, not the other one. In a legal text those two instructions are the whole meaning.

quickfire.situation: It was not the surveyor who was at fault. What does the sentence do that the surveyor was not at fault does not?
tips: It names the surveyor in order to exclude him, and it implies somebody else.
The it-cleft always points at one item and pushes the rest out of frame.

quickfire.situation: The port authority in whose waters she lay was acting for a state which had ratified both instruments. Which had ratified: the authority, the waters, or the state?
tips: The state. Which attaches to the nearest suitable noun, not always the nearest word.
Re-attaching the clause is how the wrong option is built.

quickfire.situation: Say, in exam register, that a treaty is not law just because it was agreed.
tips: Adoption alone does not give a convention legal force.
Ratification and transposition are what make it binding.

quickfire.situation: Turn this into a wh-cleft: an amendment produced the detention.
tips: What produced the detention was an amendment.
The wh-cleft delays the important item to the end.

quickfire.situation: Whose flag she flies. Can whose be used for a thing rather than a person?
tips: Yes. Whose works for things, states and organisations, not only for people.
That is why the state whose flag is correct and the state which flag is not.

quickfire.situation: In one sentence, say why two identical ships at the same berth can be bound by different rules.
tips: Because their flag states ratified different instruments.
The ship is bound by what her own registry accepted, not by what the convention says.

listenings.h: The Surveyor Who Was Not at Fault
listenings.sub: The man who signed the certificate explains what he was authorised to sign. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: I have been asked the same question by three different lawyers, and the answer has not changed. I surveyed that vessel against the regime her flag state had accepted, because that is the only regime I am authorised to survey her against. My authorisation comes from one administration and from no other. If a port on the far side of an ocean has ratified a protocol that her registry has not, that is not a defect in my survey and it is not something I am permitted to correct. What people find hard to accept is that both certificates in that argument were valid. Mine was valid under the law that appointed me. Theirs was valid under the law that controlled the water. It was the water that won, and it always is.
questions: Against which regime did he survey the vessel, and why that one?
Against the regime her flag state had accepted, because that is the only regime his authorisation allows him to survey against. His authorisation comes from one administration and from no other.
What does he say people find hard to accept?
That both certificates in the argument were valid: his under the law that appointed him, theirs under the law that controlled the water.
What is his conclusion about which one prevails?
The water wins, and it always does -- the law of the place where the ship physically is.

listenings.sub: A legal adviser on the gap between signing and enforcing. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: There are three steps and most people only know the first. A convention is adopted at the organisation, and that is the photograph everybody has seen. Then it has to be ratified, which means each state accepts to be bound by it, and the instrument only enters into force once enough of them have done so. And then, third, it has to be transposed: written into the national law of that state, with a penalty attached. A state can complete step two and never complete step three, and when that happens you have a convention that is technically in force and practically invisible. It is enforcement, not ratification, that decides what a master actually experiences. Which is why the interesting question about any flag is never what it has signed. It is what it has ever detained a ship for.
questions: What are the three steps she names?
Adoption at the organisation, ratification by each state, and transposition into that state's national law with a penalty attached.
What happens when a state completes ratification but not transposition?
You get a convention that is technically in force and practically invisible.
What does she say is the interesting question about a flag?
Not what it has signed, but what it has ever detained a ship for.

roleplays.label: Guided
roleplays.scenario: Report the case in five sentences, in this order: what the ship's registry had and had not ratified, who the surveyor answered to, what the port state had ratified, why the detention happened, and where liability finally landed. Use one cleft in the fourth sentence.

The port authority in whose waters...

roleplays.label: Semi-free
roleplays.scenario: Take the four relative clauses in the second paragraph. For each one, say out loud which noun it attaches to and how you know. Then say what the sentence would mean if it attached to the noun next to it instead.

roleplays.label: Free
roleplays.scenario: Close the text. Explain to a master who is about to sail to that port why his certificate may be valid and still not be enough, and what he can actually do about it. Then say, in one sentence, what the case shows about the difference between ratification and enforcement.
roleplays.note: No support. Target: at least two clefts, and the words jurisdiction, compliance and enforcement used correctly.

pc_desc: The vocabulary of maritime law and the two structures that decide which noun a clause is about. Key words: compliance, liability, jurisdiction, amendment, ratification, annex, convention, protocol, provision, enforcement. Structure: cleft sentences and relative clauses with prepositions.

paras: What makes a convention law on a particular ship is ratification by the state whose flag she flies. It is for that reason that two identical vessels at the same berth may be subject to different provisions.

The classification society to which the owner had contracted the surveys held an authorisation from one flag state only. The port authority in whose waters she lay was acting for a state which had ratified both instruments. It was not the surveyor who was at fault, and what produced the detention was an amendment that one registry had accepted and the other had not.

quiz.q: It was not the surveyor who was at fault. What does this structure add?
opts: Nothing. It is a longer way of saying the surveyor was not at fault.
It names the surveyor in order to exclude him, and implies that somebody else is meant.
It means the writer is unsure who was at fault.

quiz.q: The port authority in whose waters she lay was acting for a state which had ratified both instruments. Who had ratified both?
opts: The port authority.
The state the authority was acting for.
The vessel's own flag state.

quiz.q: Why is it the state whose flag she flies and not the state which flag she flies?
opts: Because whose shows possession, and it works for states as well as for people.
Because which can never introduce a relative clause.
Because a state is treated as a person in legal English.

teacher.s1: Abertura (2 min): DECISAO DE DESENHO do programa: toda aula e reading-driven, sem alternar com aula de fala (a REGRA 29.2 nao se aplica aqui), porque a prova e 100% leitura. Entre direto, sem cumprimento scriptado (REGRA 27A). Comeca o bloco 2: os textos ficam mais dificeis, nao mais longos.
teacher.s2: Homework check + warm-up (5 min): Ela escreveu dez frases originais com as palavras do bloco 1 em que ainda hesitava. Peca tres. O que voce mede: erro de COLOCACAO (palavra certa, companhia errada) e o que sobra num B2 -- anote quais e leve para o capitulo 5.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (5 min): A frase esta gramaticalmente perfeita e factualmente impossivel. Espere ela achar. Se travar, pergunte: can a ship be registered to a port authority? A resposta e nao -- e o problema e a que substantivo a oracao se prende.
teacher.s4: Objetivo (2 min): Diga: the words of the law, the two ways English points at things, and which noun a clause belongs to.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words, and none of them is about the sea. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (5 min): compliance, liability, jurisdiction, amendment. NAO traduza (REGRA 13). CCQ para liability: Is liability the same as fault? (NAO -- e o ponto do texto: liability seguiu a bandeira, nao a culpa.) CCQ para jurisdiction: Can two states have jurisdiction over the same ship at the same time? (Sim, e e exatamente o caso.)
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (5 min): ratification, annex, convention. CCQ para ratification: Does ratification make the rule work on board? (Nao sozinha -- falta a transposicao. O listening 2 fecha isso.) Diga que annex e onde moram as regras tecnicas -- os artigos sao so o esqueleto.
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (5 min): protocol, provision, enforcement. CCQ para protocol: Is a protocol a new convention? (Nao -- e um instrumento que ADICIONA ou MODIFICA uma convencao existente. E a distincao que causou a detencao no texto.) CCQ para enforcement: Who does enforcement in this text? (O porto, nao a bandeira.)
teacher.s9: Consolidate (4 min): Ela toca a palavra e le a definicao em voz alta antes de fechar o par.
teacher.s10: Transicao leitura (1 min): Diga: Three legal systems, one hull, and everybody is right. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: a pergunta ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Leitura (7 min): Tres minutos em silencio, sem dicionario. NAO traduza. Este e o texto mais denso ate aqui -- avise que releitura de frase e normal e nao e fracasso. Depois UMA frase de resumo.
teacher.s12: Gist (3 min): Ela escolhe e JUSTIFICA. A opcao (c) e a leitura intuitiva e errada: o texto diz explicitamente que o comandante nao tinha culpa.
teacher.s13: True or False (7 min): REGRA DA CASA: TRUE ou FALSE e DEPOIS a linha que prova. A afirmacao 5 troca FLAG state por PORT state -- e o erro de referencia que a aula inteira treina.
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: Now the two structures that made that text hard. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (7 min): Nao de a regra. Peca que ela reescreva os exemplos 1 e 2 em ordem normal e diga o que se perde. Depois, nos exemplos 3 e 4, pergunte a QUE substantivo a oracao se prende. So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ decisivo: in 'a state which had ratified both', which points at the state or at the waters? Ela estuda gramatica sozinha: aqui e ferramenta de leitura.
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela diz a forma ORALMENTE antes de clicar.
teacher.s17: Spot the error (4 min): Os quatro: which por who em pessoa, concordancia no wh-cleft, preposicao orfa no fim com pronome repetido, e which flag por whose flag.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same case, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (4 min): O quarto par (liability followed the flag) e o que muda QUEM responde -- e o tipo de troca que decide questao.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (5 min): Depois de fechar os pares, cubra a direita e faca a direcao dificil.
teacher.s21: Complete (5 min): Teacher-led, uma lacuna por vez. As oito respostas sao oito das dez palavras da aula.
teacher.s22: Quick fire (6 min): Uma por vez, em voz alta, antes das dicas. A segunda (which had ratified) e a que treina o defeito do slide 3.
teacher.s23: Transicao (1 min): Diga: The man who signed, and the lawyer who explains why it did not matter. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening 1 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Escuta medida em 0%: 0.75x na primeira vez. No fim pergunte: he says both certificates were valid. Does the written text agree? (Concorda -- e a frase 'Both readings were correct'.)
teacher.s25: Listening 2 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Este audio da os TRES passos (adoption, ratification, transposition) que o texto so insinua. Peca que ela repita os tres sem olhar.
teacher.s26: Role-play guiado (4 min): Cinco frases com os frames. Conte quantas oracoes relativas corretas ela produz.
teacher.s27: Role-play semi-livre (5 min): O exercicio e apontar o substantivo e DIZER COMO SABE. 'Porque faz sentido' nao basta: exija o criterio (concordancia, sentido, posicao).
teacher.s28: Producao livre (6 min): Nao interrompa. Mede-se: dois clefts e o uso correto de jurisdiction, compliance e enforcement.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Let us see what you can do now.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases do proprio texto. Insista na pronuncia de 'liability' (lai-a-BIL-i-ti) e 'jurisdiction' (jur-is-DIC-shun).
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Lesson 6 complete, Helena.
